title: Pearson Edexcel GCSE (9–1) History Specification
subtitle: Option P1: Spain and the ‘New World’, c1490–c1555

exam_structure.overview: Tests unfolding period narrative across 3 Key Topics. Q1 Explain two consequences (8m), Q2 Write an analytical narrative (8m), Q3 Explain the importance of two events (16m).

sections.title: Key topic 1: Spain reaches the Americas, c1490–1512

topics.title: 1. Spanish exploration
points: Spain c1490: the crusading spirit and foreign ambitions.
Columbus’s attempts to gain sponsorship. The role of Queen Isabella: her desire to spread Christianity and sponsorship of Columbus.
Columbus’s first voyage of 1492 and the problems encountered.

topics.title: 2. Columbus reaches the Americas
points: Columbus’s actions: exploration of the Bahamas and the Caribbean. The foundation of La Navidad.
The impact of contact with Indigenous peoples: the discovery of gold, relations with the Tainos and Caribs.
The impact of rivalry with Portugal, and the Treaty of Tordesillas (1494).

topics.title: 3. Spanish claims in the Caribbean
points: Columbus’s later voyages and his role as governor in the Spanish settlement. The significance of the establishment of the Spanish colony at Santo Domingo (1496).
The effects of Spanish settlement: treatment of Indigenous peoples, effects of smallpox.

Development of an imperial policy in relation to the Caribbean: the regulation of further exploration, the establishment of a monopoly on trade, the extension of Spanish authority and the use of slavery. The role of Catholic missionaries.

topics.title: 1. The start of an empire
points: Balboa’s claim of Spanish authority over the Pacific (1513).
The conquest of Cuba.
The voyage of Magellan and Spanish claim to the Philippines.

topics.title: 2. The conquest of Mexico
points: Cortes’s expedition to Mexico in 1519.
Key events of the Spanish conquest of Mexico; the role of Montezuma, the war between Aztecs and Tlaxcalans.
The capture of Tenochtitlan and the Aztec surrender.

topics.title: 3. Impact of Spain in the Americas
points: Cortes’s actions as Governor and Captain-General of New Spain (1523–28).
The consequences of the Spanish invasion for the Aztecs.
The founding and significance of a Spanish base at Panama.

sections.title: Key topic 3: The Spanish Empire c1528–c1555

topics.title: 1. Pizarro and the conquest of the Incas
points: Contact with the Incas (1528); the significance of the death of Huayna Capac.
The voyage of Pizarro (1530), and the significance of the war between Atahuallpa and Huascar.
Key events of the Spanish conquest of Peru: the Battle of Cajamarca and the capture of Atahuallpa, the revolt of the Incas, the siege of Cuzco (1536–37). The impact of the conquest.

topics.title: 2. Expansion of empire
points: The role of the viceroys and encomiendas in the Spanish Empire. The role of Las Casas and the significance of the New Laws (1542).
The significance of the discovery of silver in Bolivia and in Mexico. The foundation of La Paz (1548).

topics.title: 3. Impact of the 'New World' on Spain
points: The importance of gold and silver for the Spanish economy and to support Spain’s European empire.
The impact on Spain of the slave trade and goods from the Americas.
The government of the Spanish Empire: the role of the House of Trade and Council of the Indies.
